name: Supporting (sustentacular) cell of the dog's nose
blurb: The tall supporting cell of a dog's smell lining: a column topped with a fur of microvilli, with its nucleus near the top and a thin foot reaching down to the base, standing between the smell neurons.
note: Model: a supporting (sustentacular) cell from the smell lining of the dog's nose, cut in half. Measured, in dogs and in other mammals as named in the sources: the cell's place and job, that it carries microvilli on its free face, that its nucleus lies toward the top of the lining, that it is joined to its neighbours by junctions, and that it partly wraps the dendrites of the smell neurons. Illustrative, because no source read for this model gives it for the dog: the height, the width, the taper, the length of the microvilli, the size and shape of the nucleus, the number of junctions and organelles, and all colours. The neurons around the cell are not drawn.

height.note: illustrative. A review of nasal anatomy gives the whole olfactory lining as about 60 µm tall (gizurarsson2012; the sentence does not name the species), and a study of beagle noses found the dog's olfactory lining thicker than a rabbit's by 39.9 µm on average (yang2026), but no source read gives the dog's lining or its supporting cell as a number. The cell is drawn as tall as the lining.

width_at_top.calc: drawn width of 8 µm at the base times a taper of 1.8, rounded
width_at_top.note: illustrative; the cell is wider where the nucleus lies than at its foot

microvillus_length.note: illustrative; the microvilli are known to reach up into the mucus and to meet the cilia of the smell neurons there (elsevier_atlas), but no length for the dog was read

neurons_per_supporting_cell.note: not given: only that supporting cells outnumber the smell neurons in the dog (anatomyatlases)

nucleus.note: One oval nucleus lies in the upper part of the cell, in the top layer of nuclei of the lining, above the nuclei of the smell neurons (in the dog the neuron nuclei lie deep, anatomyatlases). That the nucleus of a supporting cell lies higher than the others is from a review of the human nose (gizurarsson2012); the same crowded, high position is described in the wolf's vomeronasal organ (wolf2024). Its size, shape and the one nucleolus are illustrative.

volume_fraction.note: illustrative; the cell is said to be rich in mitochondria (gizurarsson2012), but no share was read

count.note: illustrative; pigment (lipofuscin) granules are known in these cells (gizurarsson2012), their number and size are not

not_drawn: the actin core of each microvillus
the smell neurons and the basal cells around it
the cell's thin extensions that wrap the neurons' fibres near the base

special.note: Many microvilli stand on the free face and reach into the mucus, where they meet the cilia of the smell neurons (elsevier_atlas). Their count, length and thickness here are illustrative; only the fingers on the cut and the visible face are drawn.

The dendrite of a smell neuron often lies in a groove or pocket of a supporting cell, which partly or wholly wraps it; this was shown in mouse, rat and human (liang2020), and the dog's lining is likely to be the same, though no dog source was read. Two wrapped dendrites are drawn at the top of the cell; the number is illustrative.

Near the free face the cell is bound to its neighbours and to the smell neurons by junctions (elsevier_atlas, liang2020). Drawn as a ring just under the microvilli, thicker than in life. A review of the human nose states that the seal to the neurons is not a gap or tight junction (gizurarsson2012); the sources differ on the kind of junction, so the ring stands for the belt of junctions as a whole.
Desmosomes join neighbouring supporting cells near the free face (elsevier_atlas). 40 are drawn, an illustrative number.

The cell reaches from the free surface to the base of the lining; in the dog the smell neurons lie between the supporting cells (anatomyatlases). The narrowing of the lower part into a thin foot is illustrative.

cut: The cell is cut in half lengthwise: a tall column, wider near the top where the oval nucleus lies and narrowing toward a thin foot; microvilli stand on the free face, a ring of junctions lies just below them, mitochondria and pigment granules lie through the cytoplasm, and the neighbouring cells show faintly beside it; two wrapped dendrites of smell neurons lie in grooves near the top.

colours.convention: Cell membrane pale peach, the inside dark; microvilli pale straw; the ring of junctions and the desmosomes brown; nucleus violet; mitochondria orange; pigment granules yellow-brown; the wrapped dendrites pale blue. None of these is a real colour: all are a code.

cytosol.name: Cytosol
cytosol.about: The watery inside of the cell, crowded with proteins. In this cell it forms a tall column, widest where the nucleus lies.

microvillus.name: Microvillus
microvillus.about: A finger of the cell surface. Its surface is membrane over a core of actin, a protein; the closer view shows a protein as a stand-in for that actin core.

wrapped_dendrite.name: Wrapped dendrite of a smell neuron
wrapped_dendrite.about: A thin fibre of a smell neuron, the dendrite that carries its knob of cilia to the surface. The closer view is that smell neuron.

granule.name: Pigment granule (lipofuscin)
granule.about: A small granule of worn-out cell material (it is an aggregate of damaged protein and lipid; the closer view shows a protein as a stand-in, since no view of lipofuscin itself is built) that builds up in the cell and shows as a yellowish-brown pigment. Supporting cells of the smell lining are known to carry such granules, which give the lining a faint yellow-brown tint.

basal_process.name: Thin foot of the cell
basal_process.about: The lower end of the cell narrows into a thin foot that reaches toward the base of the lining, where new cells are made from stem cells. Its shape is illustrative.

neighbour.name: Neighbouring cell of the smell lining

about: This is the supporting cell of the smell lining in a dog's nose. In the dog these cells are more numerous than the smell neurons that lie between them (anatomyatlases), and the cell stands from the free surface down to the base of the lining. The drawn cell is {drawn.cellVolume} µm³; its height and width are illustrative, since no source read gives them for the dog.

Its microvilli reach into the mucus above, where they meet the cilia of the smell neurons; neighbouring cells are joined by desmosomes and by junctions near the free face (elsevier_atlas). The cell partly wraps the dendrites of the smell neurons (liang2020), which is why it is called a supporting cell: reviews of the dog's nose add that it helps set the make-up of the mucus, insulates the neurons from one another and protects the lining from what is breathed in (frontvet2018), and that it takes up dead neurons (canine_review2021).

The nucleus ({drawn.nuclei} drawn) lies high in the lining, above the nuclei of the neurons. Neurons here live for only weeks and are replaced from basal cells, which can also become supporting cells (canine_review2021); supporting cells in three beagles stain for the epithelial markers SOX2 and cytokeratin (yoshida2024). Most of the structure comes from other mammals, as each note says; the sizes are illustrative.
